$comment: SCIMServer estate registry - the single source of truth for WHERE the estates are.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS.
The dev + canary-prod estates live on an EPHEMERAL Azure AD tenant that expires
roughly every 80 days, so they are rebuilt in a new tenant 4 to 5 times a year.
Before this file, estate identity was smeared across ~30 files (scripts, gates,
prompts, Playwright specs, docs) and each rollover meant a repo-wide find-and-
replace. The 2026-08-12 rollover took 97 replacements across 28 files, and that
bulk edit silently rewrote the RETIRING tenant's entry in the tenant map to the
NEW tenant's ids - corrupting the one file whose job is to hold both apart. No
gate caught it. The fix is not a better gate; it is to stop doing bulk identity
replaces at all.
TWO RULES THAT SHAPE THE SCHEMA.
1. NEVER store an FQDN. The Container Apps environment domain (purplecliff-91e4026d,
previously proudbush-ae90986e, before that yellowsmoke-af7a3fff) is ASSIGNED BY
AZURE at environment-creation time. It is unknowable until the environment
exists and different every time. A stored FQDN is a value guaranteed to become
false. Resolve it at run time with:
az containerapp show -n <app> -g <rg> --query properties.configuration.ingress.fqdn -o tsv
scim-estates.ps1 does this for you via Get-ScimEstateFqdn.
2. ADDRESS BY ROLE, NOT BY NAME. Scripts ask for 'the active dev estate', never
for 'scimserver-dev.purplecliff-91e4026d...'. A rollover then becomes a role
reassignment in this file rather than an edit to every consumer.
ROLE VOCABULARY (finite and typed on purpose - this must not grow into a DSL):
active     the estate currently serving as dev / canary prod. Every gate,
pipeline and prompt targets this.
next       provisioned and being filled, not yet cut over.
retiring   superseded. Kept intact deliberately; may be unmanageable if its
subscription has expired (ARM dies, the PostgreSQL data plane does not).
permanent  customer-facing production. Never rotates, never auto-promoted,
lives in its own tenant, and is excluded from every automated flow.
trial      a throwaway estate used to PROVE a replication run before it is
trusted with dev or prod. Deleted afterwards.
SECRETS ARE NOT STORED HERE. Service principal credentials live in
~/.scimserver-deploy/<tenant>.json and auth-proof identities in
~/.scimserver-deploy/<tenant>-authproofs.json, both outside the repository.
REVISION RETENTION (revisionKeep).
How many ACTIVE Container Apps revisions each estate retains after a deploy.
An active revision at 0% traffic is not free: it still runs a replica holding a
Prisma connection pool. Measured on proudbush 2026-07-31: 13 active revisions,
12 idle, 65 connections of demand against a max_connections of 50.
The DEFAULT is 2 - the revision serving traffic plus one previous revision as an
instant rollback target. Dropping to 1 halves the always-on compute for that
estate and REMOVES the rollback target, so recovery becomes roll-forward only.
That is a real trade, so any estate below 2 MUST carry a revisionKeepRationale
and the validator (R8) rejects the registry otherwise. Only a customer-prod
estate may go below 2, because it is the one estate never auto-promoted - every
deployment to it is a deliberate, supervised act.

tenants.notes: Ephemeral. Expect replacement around 2026-11. directoryAccessGranted means the deploy SP holds the Graph role Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy, so app-registration work needs no interactive sign-in.

ARM control plane EXPIRED 2026-08-11 (AADSTS5000229). The apps still serve and the PostgreSQL data plane still accepts connections, but nothing can be managed, patched or deleted. Two subscriptions share the NAME ProvIAM_Subscription, so always resolve by subscriptionId.

tenants.tenantDomain: (not captured - the deployment SP has no directory read)
tenants.notes: Customer-facing production. Separate permanent tenant, so it cannot pull from the ProvIAM-tenant ACR and uses anonymous GHCR instead. Never auto-promoted. directoryAccessGranted is deliberately false - see grant-deploy-sp-directory-access.ps1, which refuses this tenant.

estates.notes: The managed environment lives in the OTHER resource group (scimserver-prod) because Azure allows only one Container Apps environment per subscription per region. The app must therefore reference it by full resourceId - passing a bare name only searches the target resource group.
Same tenant as dev, so it can be auto-promoted as a true blue/green canary. Multiple-revision mode.

estates.revisionKeepRationale: Cost. This estate runs on an MSDN offer with a USD 150/month credit and hit the spending limit on 2026-08-14, which disabled the subscription until the next billing period. An active revision at 0% traffic still runs an always-on replica (0.5 vCPU / 1 GiB), so the second revision was roughly a third of the estate's entire compute bill for a rollback path that has never been exercised here. Keeping 1 removes the instant-rollback target: recovery is ROLL FORWARD - re-run promote-to-prod.ps1 with the previous image tag, which is always available from GHCR. Acceptable specifically here because this estate is never auto-promoted, so every deployment to it is deliberate and supervised, and because the canary prod estate has already proven the same image before it ever reaches this one.
estates.notes: NEVER auto-promoted. Requires an explicit operator go-ahead and its own az login into the AnandSa tenant.
Still serving on the expired tenant. Read-only in practice: ARM cannot reach it. Retained so its data plane stays addressable.
Still serving on the expired tenant. Same constraints as dev-retiring.
